sanskrit: manīṣiṇo hi ye ke cid yatayo mokṣakāṅkṣiṇaḥ teṣāṃ vai chinnatṛṣṇānāṃ yogakṣemavaho hariḥ
english: For all those wise ascetics who long for liberation, who have severed every craving, it is Hari who bears their welfare and their gain.

sanskrit: jāyamānaṃ hi puruṣaṃ yaṃ paśyen madhusūdanaḥ sāttvikas tu sa vijñeyo bhaven mokṣe ca niścitaḥ
english: Whatever man, at his very birth, Madhusūdana looks upon, that man is to be known as endowed with sattva and assured of liberation.

sanskrit: sāṃkhyayogena tulyo hi dharma ekāntasevitaḥ nārāyaṇātmake mokṣe tato yānti parāṃ gatim
english: This dharma practised with single-minded devotion is equal in worth to Sāṃkhya and Yoga; through it men attain the supreme goal, the liberation whose very self is Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: nārāyaṇena dṛṣṭaś ca pratibuddho bhavet pumān evam ātmecchayā rājan pratibuddho na jāyate
english: The man whom Nārāyaṇa beholds is awakened to truth; but one awakened by his own will alone, O king, is not so awakened.

sanskrit: rājasī tāmasī caiva vyāmiśre prakṛtī smṛte tadātmakaṃ hi puruṣaṃ jāyamānaṃ viśāṃ pate pravṛttilakṣaṇair yuktaṃ nāvekṣati hariḥ svayam
english: The rājasic and tāmasic natures are remembered to be intermingled; and the man whose self is composed of these, O lord of peoples, born marked by the signs of worldly engagement, Hari himself does not regard.

sanskrit: paśyaty enaṃ jāyamānaṃ brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ rajasā tamasā caiva mānuṣaṃ samabhiplutam
english: It is Brahmā, the grandsire of the worlds, who looks upon such a man at his birth—the mortal flooded over by rajas and tamas.

sanskrit: kāmaṃ devāś ca ṛṣayaḥ sattvasthā nṛpasattama hīnāḥ sattvena sūkṣmeṇa tato vaikārikāḥ smṛtāḥ
english: True, the gods and the sages abide in sattva, O best of kings; yet, lacking that subtle sattva, they are accordingly remembered as belonging to the modified order.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca kathaṃ vaikāriko gacchet puruṣaḥ puruṣottamam
english: Janamejaya said: How can a man of the modified order attain the Supreme Person?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca susūkṣmasattvasaṃyuktaṃ saṃyuktaṃ tribhir akṣaraiḥ puruṣaḥ puruṣaṃ gacchen niṣkriyaḥ pañcaviṃśakam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Joined to the most subtle sattva, joined to the three syllables, the man, ceasing from action, attains that Person, the twenty-fifth principle.

sanskrit: evam ekaṃ sāṃkhyayogaṃ vedāraṇyakam eva ca parasparāṅgāny etāni pañcarātraṃ ca kathyate eṣa ekāntināṃ dharmo nārāyaṇaparātmakaḥ
english: Thus Sāṃkhya and Yoga are one, and so too the Veda and the Āraṇyaka; these, together with the Pañcarātra, are declared to be limbs of one another. This is the dharma of the single-minded devotees, whose supreme Self is Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: yathā samudrāt prasṛtā jalaughās; tam eva rājan punar āviśanti ime tathā jñānamahājalaughā; nārāyaṇaṃ vai punar āviśanti
english: As the floods of water gone forth from the ocean enter again, O king, that very ocean, so the great floods of knowledge enter again into Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: eṣa te kathito dharmaḥ sātvato yadubāndhava kuruṣvainaṃ yathānyāyaṃ yadi śaknoṣi bhārata
english: This Sātvata dharma has been told to you, O kinsman of the Yadus; observe it as is fitting, if you are able, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: evaṃ hi sumahābhāgo nārado gurave mama śvetānāṃ yatinām āha ekāntagatim avyayām
english: For thus did the greatly blessed Nārada declare to my teacher the imperishable, single-minded goal of the white-robed ascetics.

sanskrit: vyāsaś cākathayat prītyā dharmaputrāya dhīmate sa evāyaṃ mayā tubhyam ākhyātaḥ prasṛto guroḥ
english: And Vyāsa, out of affection, recounted it to the wise son of Dharma; that very teaching, descended from my teacher, I have now set forth to you.

sanskrit: itthaṃ hi duścaro dharma eṣa pārthivasattama yathaiva tvaṃ tathaivānye na bhajanti vimohitāḥ
english: Hard to follow, indeed, is this dharma, O best of kings; even as you do, so others do not embrace it, for they are bewildered.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇa eva hi lokānāṃ bhāvano mohanas tathā saṃhārakārakaś caiva kāraṇaṃ ca viśāṃ pate
english: For Kṛṣṇa alone is the creator of the worlds, their bewilderer, and their destroyer too, and their very cause, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca sāṃkhyaṃ yogaṃ pañcarātraṃ vedāraṇyakam eva ca jñānāny etāni brahmarṣe lokeṣu pracaranti ha
english: Janamejaya said: Sāṃkhya, Yoga, the Pañcarātra, and the Veda with its Āraṇyaka—these bodies of knowledge, O brahmin sage, are current among the worlds.

sanskrit: kim etāny ekaniṣṭhāni pṛthaṅniṣṭhāni vā mune prabrūhi vai mayā pṛṣṭaḥ pravṛttiṃ ca yathākramam
english: Do these rest upon a single foundation, or upon separate foundations, O sage? Being asked by me, declare it, and their origin in due order.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca jajñe bahujñaṃ param atyudāraṃ; yaṃ dvīpamadhye sutam ātmavantam parāśarād gandhavatī maharṣiṃ; tasmai namo 'jñānatamonudāya
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: To that great sage, knowing many things, supreme and most noble, the self-possessed son whom Gandhavatī bore to Parāśara on the island—to him, dispeller of the darkness of ignorance, be salutation.

sanskrit: pitāmahādyaṃ pravadanti ṣaṣṭhaṃ; maharṣim ārṣeyavibhūtiyuktam nārāyaṇasyāṃśajam ekaputraṃ; dvaipāyanaṃ vedamahānidhānam
english: They declare him the sixth, counting from the Grandsire, the great sage endowed with the glory of the seers, born of a portion of Nārāyaṇa, the only son, Dvaipāyana, the great treasure-house of the Veda.

sanskrit: tam ādikāleṣu mahāvibhūtir; nārāyaṇo brahmamahānidhānam sasarja putrārtham udāratejā; vyāsaṃ mahātmānam ajaḥ purāṇaḥ
english: Him, in the primal ages, did Nārāyaṇa of mighty majesty, the great treasure-house of the Brahman, create for the sake of a son—the unborn, the ancient one of lofty splendour, brought forth the great-souled Vyāsa.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca tvayaiva kathitaḥ pūrvaṃ saṃbhavo dvijasattama vasiṣṭhasya sutaḥ śaktiḥ śakteḥ putraḥ parāśaraḥ
english: Janamejaya said: By you yourself was his lineage told before, O best of the twice-born: Śakti was the son of Vasiṣṭha, and Parāśara the son of Śakti.

sanskrit: parāśarasya dāyādaḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyano muniḥ bhūyo nārāyaṇasutaṃ tvam evainaṃ prabhāṣase
english: The heir of Parāśara was the sage Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana; yet now you speak of this same one as the son of Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: kim ataḥ pūrvajaṃ janma vyāsasyāmitatejasaḥ kathayasvottamamate janma nārāyaṇodbhavam
english: What, then, is the earlier birth of Vyāsa of measureless splendour? Tell me, O man of excellent mind, of his birth that sprang from Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca vedārthān vettukāmasya dharmiṣṭhasya taponidheḥ guror me jñānaniṣṭhasya himavatpāda āsataḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: While my teacher, most righteous, a treasury of austerity, fixed upon knowledge, longing to understand the meanings of the Vedas, was dwelling at the foot of the Himālaya—

sanskrit: kṛtvā bhāratam ākhyānaṃ tapaḥśrāntasya dhīmataḥ śuśrūṣāṃ tatparā rājan kṛtavanto vayaṃ tadā
english: having composed the tale of the Bhārata, the wise one was wearied with austerity; and we, O king, intent upon it, rendered him our devoted service in those days.

sanskrit: sumantur jaiminiś caiva pailaś ca sudṛḍhavrataḥ ahaṃ caturthaḥ śiṣyo vai śuko vyāsātmajas tathā
english: Sumantu, and Jaimini, and Paila of firm vows, I myself the fourth disciple, and Śuka, the son of Vyāsa—

sanskrit: ebhiḥ parivṛto vyāsaḥ śiṣyaiḥ pañcabhir uttamaiḥ śuśubhe himavatpāde bhūtair bhūtapatir yathā
english: surrounded by these five excellent disciples, Vyāsa shone at the foot of the Himālaya like the Lord of beings amid his attendant spirits.

sanskrit: vedān āvartayan sāṅgān bhāratārthāṃś ca sarvaśaḥ tam ekamanasaṃ dāntaṃ yuktā vayam upāsmahe
english: As he recited the Vedas together with their auxiliaries, and the meanings of the Bhārata in every part, we, attentive, waited upon him, the single-minded, the self-controlled.

sanskrit: kathāntare 'tha kasmiṃś cit pṛṣṭo 'smābhir dvijottamaḥ vedārthān bhāratārthāṃś ca janma nārāyaṇāt tathā
english: Then, in the course of some discourse, that best of the twice-born was asked by us about the meanings of the Vedas, the meanings of the Bhārata, and his birth from Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: sa pūrvam uktvā vedārthān bhāratārthāṃś ca tattvavit nārāyaṇād idaṃ janma vyāhartum upacakrame
english: He, the knower of truth, having first spoken of the meanings of the Vedas and of the Bhārata, then set about to relate this birth of his from Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: śṛṇudhvam ākhyānavaram etad ārṣeyam uttamam ādikālodbhavaṃ viprās tapasādhigataṃ mayā
english: Hear this excellent tale, supreme, belonging to the seers, arising in primal time, O brahmins, attained by me through austerity.

sanskrit: prāpte prajāvisarge vai saptame padmasaṃbhave nārāyaṇo mahāyogī śubhāśubhavivarjitaḥ
english: When the time of the creation of creatures had come, in the seventh, the birth from the lotus, Nārāyaṇa, the great yogin, free of good and evil alike—

sanskrit: sasṛje nābhitaḥ putraṃ brahmāṇam amitaprabham tataḥ sa prādurabhavad athainaṃ vākyam abravīt
english: created from his navel a son, Brahmā of boundless radiance; thereupon that one came forth, and to him he spoke these words:

sanskrit: mama tvaṃ nābhito jātaḥ prajāsargakaraḥ prabhuḥ sṛja prajās tvaṃ vividhā brahman sajaḍapaṇḍitāḥ
english: "You are born from my navel, the lord and maker of the creation of creatures; create manifold beings, O Brahman, both the dull and the wise."

sanskrit: sa evam ukto vimukhaś cintāvyākulamānasaḥ praṇamya varadaṃ devam uvāca harim īśvaram
english: Thus addressed, he turned away, his mind troubled with anxious thought; and bowing to the boon-granting god, he said to Hari, the Lord:

sanskrit: kā śaktir mama deveśa prajāḥ sraṣṭuṃ namo 'stu te aprajñāvān ahaṃ deva vidhatsva yad anantaram
english: "What power have I, O Lord of the gods, to create creatures? Homage be to you. I am without the requisite wisdom, O god; ordain what is to follow."

sanskrit: sa evam ukto bhagavān bhūtvāthāntarhitas tataḥ cintayām āsa deveśo buddhiṃ buddhimatāṃ varaḥ
english: Thus addressed, the Blessed One then vanished from sight, and the Lord of the gods, the foremost of the wise, called to mind Buddhi, the faculty of intellect.

sanskrit: svarūpiṇī tato buddhir upatasthe hariṃ prabhum yogena caināṃ niryogaḥ svayaṃ niyuyuje tadā
english: Then Buddhi, having taken visible form, presented herself before the Lord Hari; and he, the unattached, himself joined her by his power of yoga.

sanskrit: sa tām aiśvaryayogasthāṃ buddhiṃ śaktimatīṃ satīm uvāca vacanaṃ devo buddhiṃ vai prabhur avyayaḥ
english: To that Buddhi, established in the yoga of sovereign power, mighty and true, the imperishable Lord, the god, spoke these words:

sanskrit: brahmāṇaṃ praviśasveti lokasṛṣṭyarthasiddhaye tatas tam īśvarādiṣṭā buddhiḥ kṣipraṃ viveśa sā
english: "Enter into Brahmā, for the accomplishing of the world's creation." Then, commanded by the Lord, Buddhi swiftly entered into him.

sanskrit: athainaṃ buddhisaṃyuktaṃ punaḥ sa dadṛśe hariḥ bhūyaś cainaṃ vacaḥ prāha sṛjemā vividhāḥ prajāḥ
english: Then Hari beheld him once more, now joined with Buddhi, and again spoke to him this word: "Create these manifold beings."

sanskrit: evam uktvā sa bhagavāṃs tatraivāntaradhīyata prāpa caiva muhūrtena svasthānaṃ devasaṃjñitam
english: Having spoken thus, the Blessed One vanished there itself, and in a single moment attained his own abode, named after the gods.

sanskrit: tāṃ caiva prakṛtiṃ prāpya ekībhāvagato 'bhavat athāsya buddhir abhavat punar anyā tadā kila
english: And reaching that very nature, Brahmā came to be one with it; thereupon, it is said, another thought arose within him again.

sanskrit: sṛṣṭā imāḥ prajāḥ sarvā brahmaṇā parameṣṭhinā daityadānavagandharvarakṣogaṇasamākulāḥ jātā hīyaṃ vasumatī bhārākrāntā tapasvinī
english: All these creatures were created by Brahmā the supreme one, thronged with hosts of Daityas, Dānavas, Gandharvas, and Rākṣasas; and this earth, the bearer of wealth, was born, pressed down by the burden and made to suffer.

sanskrit: bahavo balinaḥ pṛthvyāṃ daityadānavarākṣasāḥ bhaviṣyanti tapoyuktā varān prāpsyanti cottamān
english: "Many mighty Daityas, Dānavas, and Rākṣasas shall arise upon the earth, and engaged in austerity they shall obtain the highest boons."

sanskrit: avaśyam eva taiḥ sarvair varadānena darpitaiḥ bādhitavyāḥ suragaṇā ṛṣayaś ca tapodhanāḥ tatra nyāyyam idaṃ kartuṃ bhārāvataraṇaṃ mayā
english: "Inevitably, by all those grown arrogant through the granting of boons, the hosts of gods and the sages rich in austerity shall be oppressed; therefore it is fitting that I should there bring about the lifting of this burden."

sanskrit: atha nānāsamudbhūtair vasudhāyāṃ yathākramam nigraheṇa ca pāpānāṃ sādhūnāṃ pragraheṇa ca
english: "Then, by my various manifestations upon the earth, in due succession, by the curbing of the wicked and the upholding of the good—

sanskrit: imāṃ tapasvinīṃ satyāṃ dhārayiṣyāmi medinīm mayā hy eṣā hi dhriyate pātālasthena bhoginā
english: I shall sustain this suffering, faithful earth; for by me, in the form of the serpent abiding in the nether world, is she upheld.

sanskrit: mayā dhṛtā dhārayati jagad dhi sacarācaram tasmāt pṛthvyāḥ paritrāṇaṃ kariṣye saṃbhavaṃ gataḥ
english: Upheld by me, she in turn bears the world with all that moves and is unmoving; therefore, taking birth, I shall accomplish the deliverance of the earth."

sanskrit: evaṃ sa cintayitvā tu bhagavān madhusūdanaḥ rūpāṇy anekāny asṛjat prādurbhāvabhavāya saḥ
english: Having pondered thus, the Blessed Madhusūdana brought forth many forms, for the sake of his manifestations.

sanskrit: vārāhaṃ nārasiṃhaṃ ca vāmanaṃ mānuṣaṃ tathā ebhir mayā nihantavyā durvinītāḥ surārayaḥ
english: "The boar-form, the man-lion, the dwarf, and the human likewise—by these the unruly foes of the gods are to be destroyed by me."

sanskrit: atha bhūyo jagatsraṣṭā bhoḥśabdenānunādayan sarasvatīm uccacāra tatra sārasvato 'bhavat
english: Then again the creator of the world, making the regions resound with the sound "Bhoḥ!", uttered forth the goddess Sarasvatī; and thereupon arose the Sārasvata one.

sanskrit: apāntaratamā nāma suto vāksaṃbhavo vibhoḥ bhūtabhavyabhaviṣyajñaḥ satyavādī dṛḍhavrataḥ
english: Apāntaratamas by name, the son sprung from the speech of the Lord, knower of past, present, and future, a speaker of truth, firm in his vows.

sanskrit: tam uvāca nataṃ mūrdhnā devānām ādir avyayaḥ vedākhyāne śrutiḥ kāryā tvayā matimatāṃ vara tasmāt kuru yathājñaptaṃ mayaitad vacanaṃ mune
english: To him, bowed with his head, the imperishable first of the gods said: "By you, O best of the wise, the śruti must be set in order in the expounding of the Vedas; therefore do this my word as it has been commanded, O sage."

sanskrit: tena bhinnās tadā vedā manoḥ svāyaṃbhuve 'ntare tatas tutoṣa bhagavān haris tenāsya karmaṇā tapasā ca sutaptena yamena niyamena ca
english: By him, in the age of Svāyaṃbhuva Manu, the Vedas were then divided; and thereafter the Blessed Hari was well pleased by that work of his, and by his austerity well practised, by restraint and by observance.

sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca manvantareṣu putra tvam evaṃ lokapravartakaḥ bhaviṣyasy acalo brahmann apradhṛṣyaś ca nityaśaḥ
english: The glorious Lord said: "Through the ages of the Manus, my son, you shall thus be the setter-in-motion of the worlds—unshaken, O Brahman, and forever unassailable.

sanskrit: punas tiṣye ca saṃprāpte kuravo nāma bhāratāḥ bhaviṣyanti mahātmāno rājānaḥ prathitā bhuvi
english: And again, when the Tiṣya age has come, there shall be the Bhāratas called the Kurus, great-souled kings renowned upon the earth.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tvattaḥ prasūtānāṃ kulabhedo bhaviṣyati parasparavināśārthaṃ tvām ṛte dvijasattama
english: Among those descended from you a splitting of the line shall come to pass, ending in their mutual destruction—save for you alone, O best of the twice-born.

sanskrit: tatrāpy anekadhā vedān bhetsyase tapasānvitaḥ kṛṣṇe yuge ca saṃprāpte kṛṣṇavarṇo bhaviṣyasi
english: There too, endowed with austerity, you shall divide the Vedas in many ways; and when the Kṛṣṇa age has come, you shall be of dark hue.

sanskrit: dharmāṇāṃ vividhānāṃ ca kartā jñānakaras tathā bhaviṣyasi tapoyukto na ca rāgād vimokṣyase
english: You shall be the author of manifold dharmas and likewise a maker of knowledge, possessed of austerity; yet you shall not be freed from attachment.

sanskrit: vītarāgaś ca putras te paramātmā bhaviṣyati maheśvaraprasādena naitad vacanam anyathā
english: And a son of yours, free of all passion, shall be the Supreme Self, by the grace of Maheśvara; this word shall not prove otherwise."

sanskrit: yaṃ mānasaṃ vai pravadanti putraṃ; pitāmahasyottamabuddhiyuktam vasiṣṭham agryaṃ tapaso nidhānaṃ; yaś cāpi sūryaṃ vyatiricya bhāti
english: He whom they call the mind-born son of the Grandsire, endowed with the highest understanding—Vasiṣṭha, the foremost, the treasure-house of austerity, who shines surpassing even the sun—

sanskrit: tasyānvaye cāpi tato maharṣiḥ; parāśaro nāma mahāprabhāvaḥ pitā sa te vedanidhir variṣṭho; mahātapā vai tapaso nivāsaḥ kānīnagarbhaḥ pitṛkanyakāyāṃ; tasmād ṛṣes tvaṃ bhavitā ca putraḥ
english: and in his line, thereafter, the great sage named Parāśara, of mighty power—he, your father, the most excellent treasury of the Veda, of great austerity, the very dwelling-place of penance, born of a maiden upon his father's daughter; of that seer you shall be the son.

sanskrit: bhūtabhavyabhaviṣyāṇāṃ chinnasarvārthasaṃśayaḥ ye hy atikrāntakāḥ pūrvaṃ sahasrayugaparyayāḥ
english: You, in whom every doubt about all matters of past, present, and future is severed—those thousand-yuga cycles that have passed away before,

sanskrit: tāṃś ca sarvān mayoddiṣṭān drakṣyase tapasānvitaḥ punar drakṣyasi cānekasahasrayugaparyayān
english: all those pointed out by me you shall behold, endowed with austerity; and again you shall behold the many thousand-yuga cycles to come.

sanskrit: anādinidhanaṃ loke cakrahastaṃ ca māṃ mune anudhyānān mama mune naitad vacanam anyathā
english: And me, without beginning or end in the world, bearing the discus in my hand, O sage—through meditation upon me, O sage, this word shall not prove otherwise."

sanskrit: śanaiścaraḥ sūryaputro bhaviṣyati manur mahān tasmin manvantare caiva saptarṣigaṇapūrvakaḥ tvam eva bhavitā vatsa matprasādān na saṃśayaḥ
english: "Śanaiścara, the son of Sūrya, shall become the great Manu; and in that age of the Manu, foremost among the host of the Seven Seers, you yourself shall be, my dear child, by my grace—of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca evaṃ sārasvatam ṛṣim apāntaratamaṃ tadā uktvā vacanam īśānaḥ sādhayasvety athābravīt
english: Vyāsa said: Having spoken thus to the Sārasvata sage Apāntaratamas, the Lord then said, "Go now and accomplish it."

sanskrit: so 'haṃ tasya prasādena devasya harimedhasaḥ apāntaratamā nāma tato jāto ''jñayā hareḥ punaś ca jāto vikhyāto vasiṣṭhakulanandanaḥ
english: And I, by the grace of that god of Hari's own wisdom, was thus born by the name Apāntaratamas at the command of Hari; and again I was born, renowned, the joy of Vasiṣṭha's line.

sanskrit: tad etat kathitaṃ janma mayā pūrvakam ātmanaḥ nārāyaṇaprasādena tathā nārāyaṇāṃśajam
english: Thus has this former birth of my own been told by me, brought about by the grace of Nārāyaṇa, and born of a portion of Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: mayā hi sumahat taptaṃ tapaḥ paramadāruṇam purā matimatāṃ śreṣṭhāḥ parameṇa samādhinā
english: For I performed a most mighty austerity, exceedingly severe, in days of old, O best of the wise, with the highest concentration.

sanskrit: etad vaḥ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ yan māṃ pṛcchatha putrakāḥ pūrvajanma bhaviṣyaṃ ca bhaktānāṃ snehato mayā
english: All this has been told to you that you asked of me, my children—my former birth and what is to come—out of affection for the devoted.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca eṣa te kathitaḥ pūrvaṃ saṃbhavo 'smadguror nṛpa vyāsasyākliṣṭamanaso yathā pṛṣṭaḥ punaḥ śṛṇu
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: This lineage of our teacher has now been told to you, O king—of Vyāsa of untroubled mind. Now hear once more what you have asked.

sanskrit: sāṃkhyaṃ yogaṃ pañcarātraṃ vedāḥ pāśupataṃ tathā jñānāny etāni rājarṣe viddhi nānāmatāni vai
english: Sāṃkhya, Yoga, the Pañcarātra, the Vedas, and the Pāśupata likewise—know these bodies of knowledge, O royal sage, to be of differing doctrines indeed.

sanskrit: sāṃkhyasya vaktā kapilaḥ paramarṣiḥ sa ucyate hiraṇyagarbho yogasya vettā nānyaḥ purātanaḥ
english: The expounder of Sāṃkhya, it is said, is Kapila, the supreme sage; the ancient knower of Yoga is Hiraṇyagarbha, and no other.

sanskrit: apāntaratamāś caiva vedācāryaḥ sa ucyate prācīnagarbhaṃ tam ṛṣiṃ pravadantīha ke cana
english: And Apāntaratamas, it is said, is the teacher of the Vedas; some here declare that sage to be Prācīnagarbha.

sanskrit: umāpatir bhūtapatiḥ śrīkaṇṭho brahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ uktavān idam avyagro jñānaṃ pāśupataṃ śivaḥ
english: Umā's consort, the Lord of beings, Śrīkaṇṭha, the son of Brahmā—Śiva, undisturbed, declared this knowledge, the Pāśupata.

sanskrit: pañcarātrasya kṛtsnasya vettā tu bhagavān svayam sarveṣu ca nṛpaśreṣṭha jñāneṣv eteṣu dṛśyate
english: But the knower of the whole Pañcarātra is the Blessed One himself; and in all these bodies of knowledge, O best of kings, he is to be seen.

sanskrit: yathāgamaṃ yathājñānaṃ niṣṭhā nārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ na cainam evaṃ jānanti tamobhūtā viśāṃ pate
english: According to the tradition and according to the knowledge, the Lord Nārāyaṇa is the final ground; yet those become darkness do not know him thus, O lord of peoples.
